ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Four circles of radius $5 \mathrm{~cm}$ touch the sides of a square and each other, as shown in the diagram. On each side of the square, an equilateral triangle is drawn to form a four-pointed star. What is the perimeter of the star?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a central square, with 4 congruent circles inside, arranged in a 2×2 pattern; the circles are tangent to each other, and the outer circles are respectively tangent to the four sides of the square. An equilateral triangle is constructed outward on each side of the square, forming a four-pointed star. Reasoning: The radius of each circle is 5 cm, so the diameter is 10 cm. One side of the square exactly spans the diameters of two circles, so the side length of the square is 2×10=20 cm. Each equilateral triangle uses one side of the square as its base, so the three sides of each triangle are also 20 cm. The outer perimeter of the star only includes the two outer sides of each of the 4 equilateral triangles, for a total of 8 sides of length 20 cm. Therefore the perimeter is 8×20=160 cm.

raw_record.question_text: Four circles of radius $5 \mathrm{~cm}$ touch the sides of a square and each other, as shown in the diagram. On each side of the square, an equilateral triangle is drawn to form a four-pointed star. What is the perimeter of the star?

method.method_draft: From the image, note that the four congruent circles are arranged in a 2 by 2 block inside the central square, with the left and right circles tangent to the square's vertical sides and the top and bottom circles tangent to the square's horizontal sides. From the text, each circle has radius 5 cm, so each diameter is 10 cm. The side length of the square is two diameters, or 20 cm. Each side of the square is the base of an equilateral triangle, so every side of each triangle is also 20 cm. The star perimeter consists only of the two outer sides from each of the four equilateral triangles, giving 8 outer sides total. Compute 8 × 20 = 160 cm.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the central square with four outward equilateral triangles attached, one per side. First determine the square side: across the square there are two tangent circles, and each contributes one diameter; with radius 5 cm, the square side is 4r = 20 cm. Instead of counting individual star edges immediately, use a perimeter relation: each side of the original square becomes the base of an equilateral triangle, and on the exterior boundary that base is replaced by the other two equal sides of the triangle. Thus the star perimeter is twice the perimeter of the square. The square perimeter is 4 × 20 = 80 cm, so the star perimeter is 2 × 80 = 160 cm.
